scope: Male INSL3 illustration in ordinary lifespan views; no numeric patient reference or laboratory norm.
sourceFilesPolicy: Full PDFs and user-uploaded files were read in the audit workspace; they are not redistributed in this repository. Source availability below describes the actual audit access.

adult.tail: Hold terminal display height and fade between 80 and 90; no further biological trend inferred.

geometry.meaning: All values here are authored graphic coordinates. Peak 0.14 is not a measured concentration; 0.14/0.87 is not a validated infant/adult concentration ratio.
geometry.birthJoin: Shared horizontal tangent; no prenatal undershoot. The exact location of the illustrative minimum is not a claim about biological timing.
geometry.infantTail: Source-inspired decline through 200 days, followed by an illustrative smooth connection to the unchanged one-year height.

sources.title: Dynamic Changes of Reproductive Hormones in Male Minipuberty: Temporal Dissociation of Leydig and Sertoli Cell Activity
sources.availability: Complete primary PDF inspected, including original vector paths and rendered figures. No original model code or numeric coefficients acquired.
sources.population: COPENHAGEN Minipuberty Study 2016–2018; healthy term male singletons; 119 boys in postnatal follow-up, 338 postnatal serum samples, 226 postnatal INSL3 determinations. Study reports only Caucasian infants.

figure2.statistic: Modeled mean longitudinal trajectory from random-coefficient spline analysis, including umbilical cord samples. Normalized to the infant peak of each hormone variable, not to adult concentration or each participant individually.
figure2.readingMethod: Original light-blue PDF vector path, index 5 on PDF page 5; linear displayed axes. Rounded typography-derived readings, not author coefficients.

figure3.statistic: Age-specific GAMLSS median, with postnatal observations only in the fit; same cohort as Figure 2.
figure3.caption: Median and ±SD scores are provided for INSL3.
figure3.readingMethod: Original thick black vector path 2117 on PDF page 6; linear concentration axes. Methods explicitly report square-root transformation followed by back-transformation; do not square the published values again.
figure3.limit: The fitted median declines and differs materially from early empirical age-bin medians. Without raw data/model coefficients this difference cannot be fully reconstructed or ascribed to a single cause.

sources.interpretation: A decreasing Figure 3 median does not refute the distinct Figure 2 trajectory or justify eliminating the modest early rise from an educational illustration.
assayCaveats: Methods prints LOD 0.03 µg/mL, inconsistent with Figure 3/Table S1 µg/L and the assay reference; treat this as a unit discrepancy, not a 1000-fold conversion.
Below-LOD observations are represented as LOD/2 = 0.015 µg/L; a fitted late tail near this value is not an established childhood concentration.
Main text says 55/77 = 77% detectable cord samples; Table S1 gives 55/71 = 77.46%. Preserve this discrepancy.

sources.statistic: Empirical bin summaries, not exact-age median model coefficients.
sources.limit: The first 100 days have roughly 78–81% detectable samples. The pooled postnatal 47% detection rate must not be applied to early infancy alone. Bins do not establish the exact peak day.

sources.availability: Full primary text and Table 2 inspected; Methods p 4021, Table 2 p 4022, Discussion pp 4024–4025.
sources.population: Healthy control boys from Finnish and Danish birth cohorts, sampling at 2.5–3.5 months; other study groups concern cryptorchidism.
sources.assay: Serum TRFIA described in Bay 2005; LOD 0.05 ng/mL.
sources.statistic: Group medians and observed ranges, not a fitted trajectory.
sources.limit: Cord-versus-three-month comparisons do not resolve a transient first-month peak. The infant upper observed range must not be substituted for the central concentration.

sources.availability: Primary indexed PubMed abstract checked; no new complete PDF acquired. Bay 2007 explicitly links its assay to this work.
sources.limit: Infant and adult cohorts are separate. Their median ratio near 13–15% describes these groups at about three months, not the longitudinal first-month peak or a universal calibration. Adult percentile intervals differ from infant observed ranges.

sources.availability: Complete author PDF inspected; Methods pp 1869–1870, Figure 1A p 1870, Discussion pp 1872–1875.
sources.population: 1073 boys and men across reference cohorts; listed ages 10.0–60.9 years, with a recruitment gap 27.6–31.4 years. Other hCG/diurnal cohorts do not extend the healthy reference chart.
sources.limitUpdate: Discussion pp 1872–1873 explicitly lowers LOD from 0.06 to 0.03 after an additional spiking experiment and retains LOQ 0.15. Applying LOQ to Busch is an assay-reference inference; Busch does not explicitly state its INSL3 LOQ.
sources.interpretation: Supports pubertal rise and broadly high young-adult concentrations, followed by lower older-group concentrations; not a calibrated numerical splice to TRFIA studies.

sources.availability: Complete author PDF inspected; Methods pp 530–531, Results p 531, Discussion p 532.
sources.population: Selected longitudinal pilot of 10 healthy Copenhagen boys, repeated six-month visits.
sources.statistic: Tanner genital-stage group medians and observed ranges, not exact chronological-age medians.
sources.interpretation: Supports pubertal increase; authors caution against using this small pilot as a population reference. No stage-to-age mapping or numeric INSL3 patient profile activated.

sources.availability: Primary abstract and indexed Methods inspected; complete PDF not acquired during this audit.
sources.interpretation: Qualitative corroboration of pubertal rise and varying timing relative to testosterone; not a source of annual numeric medians.

sources.title: Defining the end of puberty in boys: INSL3 and the acute determinants of adult Leydig-cell functional capacity
sources.availability: Full text and the user-supplied PDF inspected; Introduction p 2, Table 1 p 4, Figure 1A/B p 5, Discussion p 7, reference 11 p 9. User file not redistributed.
sources.population: UK ALSPAC male cohort; nominal visits at 17 and 24 years.
sources.assay: TRFIA; Methods describes serum/plasma without resolving an INSL3-specific matrix.
sources.infantClaim: Introduction describes a small postnatal increase and cites Busch 2022; no independent infant data are provided.
sources.figure1B: Collated means ± SEM from several puberty/adult studies, plotted from later childhood around 9 years. An axis beginning at 0 does not establish a neonatal curve.
sources.limit: Peak around 22 years is inferred rather than directly and universally established. Do not splice group means/medians into a common calibrated lifespan concentration model.

sources.availability: Complete primary HTML/XML, Methods, Table 1, Figures 2/3 and Discussion inspected; Figure 3B medians are approximate visual readings, no author numeric age-bin table acquired.
sources.population: Community-dwelling men from eight European centres; baseline 40–79 years, follow-up mean 4.3 years, variable morbidity and lifestyle.
sources.interpretation: Cross-sectional and longitudinal results support gradual adult decline, without a sudden age-defined cliff.
sources.limit: Age-bin medians are not exact-age medians; 80–89 bin does not establish observed age 89. No complete regression intercept, exact maximum observed age or calibrated infant/adult relationship obtained.

sources.availability: Primary Methods/Results/Discussion inspected through web retrieval; publisher download blocked, no complete PDF acquired. Figure 1 was corrected 1 November 2006; no unverified old figure digitized.
sources.statistic: Cross-sectional group arithmetic means; not individual aging trajectories.
sources.interpretation: Independent support for gradual later-adult decline; no interpolation of missing group means and no concentration splice across studies.

sources.population: 12 fetal cord-serum samples at gestational weeks 15–20; distinct fetal testis samples for mRNA.
sources.assay: Older noncommercial RIA, explicitly not fully validated; cross-reactivity unknown.
sources.interpretation: Qualitative evidence of fetal presence only. Does not validate the prenatal graphic amplitude or a serum concentration peak reconstructed from mRNA.

statisticalLimits: Below-LOQ modeled medians reduce confidence in precise numerical claims. They do not prove absence of a biological wave or automatically invalidate every population estimate.
LOD/LOQ for individual assays, fitted population summaries, and display readability are different concepts. Do not silently recensor all Busch values at the external assay LOQ.
The published Figure 2 mean trajectory and Figure 3 median are distinct estimands in the same cohort. Neither can be relabeled as the other.
No common calibrated lifetime concentration model or diagnostic percentile reference is created. Laboratory norms and reference profiles of other analytes remain unchanged.
